tagline: Through the gold camps and over Banner Summit to Stanley.
intro: Idaho 21 leaves Boise up the Boise River through a basalt canyon, past Lucky Peak Dam, then climbs with Mores Creek out of the sagebrush into the ponderosa pine of the Boise National Forest and the old gold country of the Boise Basin. Past Idaho City it crosses two summits and drops 2,240 feet in switchbacks to Lowman, on the South Fork of the Payette.

From Lowman it follows the river up toward the Sawtooths and climbs to Banner Creek Summit at 7,056 feet, the divide between the Payette and the Salmon. The road comes down the far side and along the northern edge of the Sawtooths to Stanley.

moments.title: Idaho City
moments.text: In 1864 Idaho City held 7,000 people, more than Portland, and being built of wood it burned four times between 1865 and 1871.

moments.title: Lowman
moments.text: Lowman, population 44, still keeps a one-room school, and in 1989 a wildfire burned some 45,000 acres around it without injuring anyone.

moments.title: Stanley Lake
moments.text: About four miles short of Stanley a three-mile spur road leads to Stanley Lake, under the jagged 9,860-foot McGown Peak.

practical: Avalanche conditions in the Banner Summit area can close the road in winter, and the upper elevations are often closed in the winter months.
